Classes, the one you started with first

The build lives in the address bar, so 🔗 Copy Link shares it and a reload keeps it; nothing is saved. Loading a Character Builder character only reads its scores, class, and level.
The multiclassing rules, prerequisites, and spell slot tables are from the System Reference Document 5.1 by Wizards of the Coast LLC, licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License.

How multiclassing works in 5e

Each time you gain a level, you can take it in a new class instead of your current one. Your character level is the total of all your class levels, and it sets your proficiency bonus and how much experience you need. Most things a class gives, like hit points, features, and Ability Score Improvements, come from that class's own level: a fighter 4 / wizard 4 has two Ability Score Improvements, one from each class.

Prerequisites and what you gain

To take a level in a new class you need a 13 or higher in that class's key ability, and also in the key ability of every class you already have. Your starting class gives every proficiency and saving throw it lists; a class you add later gives only the ones below, and never saving throws.

ClassNeedsGained when added later
🪓 BarbarianSTR 13shields, simple weapons, martial weapons
🪕 BardCHA 13light armor, one skill, one musical instrument
✨ ClericWIS 13light armor, medium armor, shields
🌿 DruidWIS 13light armor, medium armor, shields
⚔️ FighterSTR 13 or DEX 13light armor, medium armor, shields, simple weapons, martial weapons
👊 MonkDEX 13 and WIS 13simple weapons, shortswords
🛡️ PaladinSTR 13 and CHA 13light armor, medium armor, shields, simple weapons, martial weapons
🏹 RangerDEX 13 and WIS 13light armor, medium armor, shields, simple weapons, martial weapons, one class skill
🗡️ RogueDEX 13light armor, one class skill, thieves' tools
🔥 SorcererCHA 13nothing
👁️ WarlockCHA 13light armor, simple weapons
📜 WizardINT 13nothing

Spell slots for a multiclass caster

Add your bard, cleric, druid, sorcerer, and wizard levels, plus half your paladin and ranger levels (rounded down), and look that total up on the full caster table: a cleric 3 / paladin 4 counts as a 5th-level caster and gets four 1st, three 2nd, and two 3rd-level slots. If only one of your classes has the Spellcasting feature, use that class's own table instead. Spells known and prepared are still worked out class by class, and each class can only learn spells of a level it could cast on its own; the shared slots can then cast any of them.

A warlock's Pact Magic slots stay apart from that table. They come back on a short rest, and either kind of slot can cast spells from any of your classes.

Rules that don't stack

  • Extra Attack from two classes doesn't give a third attack (only the fighter's own higher levels do that).
  • Unarmored Defense from the barbarian and the monk: once you have one, you can't gain the other.
  • Channel Divinity from the cleric and the paladin gives you both sets of options but no extra uses.
  • Cantrips that grow stronger use your character level, not one class's level.

Works with

Load a character from the Character Builder to try classes on top of it, or work out the scores first with the Point Buy Calculator. The Spellbook filters spells by class and level, and the Rules Quick Reference covers the conditions and other rules you look up mid-session.
